articles.summary: Inman: Berkshire's Q2 filing confirmed its Taylor Morrison acquisition (Inman cites $6.8 billion), raised its Lennar stake nearly 30% and took a small new D.R. Horton stake, under incoming CEO Greg Abel.
articles.why_it_matters: Taylor Morrison, the sixth-largest builder, now has Berkshire's balance sheet behind it and may need far less land-bank capital, while Berkshire's bigger Lennar stake puts a deep-pocketed holder behind a Domain relationship.

suggested_update.text: Owned by Berkshire Hathaway; the acquisition was confirmed in Berkshire's Q2 2026 filing (Inman, Aug 25, 2026, cites $6.8 billion; check the price against the filing).

articles.summary: NAHB/Wells Fargo builder sentiment fell 4 points to 25 in November, the lowest since April 2012; about 46% of builders cut prices and nearly 70% used incentives.
articles.why_it_matters: Margin pressure this broad makes smaller builders likelier to seek off-balance-sheet lot capital or renegotiate option takedowns, which affects Domain's pipeline and its credit risk.
